subject: history
title: The Treaty of Versailles 1919
welcome_lead: Enter the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles in June 1919, where the victors of WWI imposed their settlement on Germany.
meta_desc: History Causes & Effects of Wars Adventure 2: terms, reception and consequences of the Treaty of Versailles.
final_note: You have weighed the Versailles settlement. Its mix of harshness and incompleteness shaped the inter-war world.

concepts.def: Wilson (USA), Lloyd George (UK), Clemenceau (France) and Orlando (Italy) at the Paris Peace Conference.
Article 231 placing responsibility for the war on Germany and her allies.
Payments demanded from Germany, set at 132 billion gold marks by the Reparations Commission in 1921.
International body established by the Treaty, headquartered in Geneva, intended to preserve peace.
Article forbidding German military forces in the Rhineland, breached by Hitler in 1936.

walkthroughs.body_html: Germany lost about 13% of its European territory (Alsace-Lorraine to France, parts of Posen and West Prussia to Poland, including the Polish Corridor), all overseas colonies, much of its merchant marine and most of its armed forces (army limited to 100,000, no air force, no submarines). Article 231 assigned war guilt and underpinned reparations.

Wilson sought a peace based on his Fourteen Points and self-determination; Clemenceau sought security against future German aggression; Lloyd George balanced punishment with the desire to keep Germany economically viable. The result was a compromise dissatisfying to all and exposing the limits of Allied unity.

Germans regarded the treaty as a Diktat and a 'stab in the back'. Economic disruption, hyperinflation (1923) and political instability fuelled extremism. The US Senate rejected the treaty and refused to join the League. Successive German governments, culminating in Hitler's, sought revision through diplomacy and ultimately force.
